chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Dennis Sandole, teacher of Pat Martino and Coltrane
summary: Collins visited Sandole in Philadelphia to study during Nat Cole layoffs, and Sandole mixed lessons with Jehovah's Witness preaching.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Sandolee. Dennis Sandolee is a fair guitarist but a great mind. I mean he's a fair guitarist in that he doesn't confine himself to guitar. He teaches music to a saxophone player, pianists, whatever. I would go and study with Dennis if I had nine days off with Nat, and everybody would go home, I'd go to Philadelphia and stay with Dennis. And we just go through the whole thing.
So I could recognize-- when I heard Pat Martina I said, well he studied with Dennis Sandolee. I knew this. Coltrane studied with Dennis Sandolee. Yeah. He's a great mind.
The only thing -- he's in Philadelphia.

Yeah, lives in a little alley, you know, and he writes. He would write and send me material. He -- it's the most illegible writing you've ever seen in your life but the one thing that would bug me, he's a Jehovah's Witness and half -- two thirds of the lesson would be chapters of the bible. You know, he was trying to -- all Jehovah's Witnesses try to convert you, you know, this is their function in life. And it got to the point that I had to talk religion all the time with him, so -- you know. But a marvelous mind.
So now Pat Martine is one of his disciples, you know,
